verdict.rationale: Metronome documents its own /ingest endpoint for usage events, rated at up to 110,000 events per second without pre-aggregation. It also documents built-in idempotency mechanisms for safe retries. Backdating of late or historical events is not evidenced anywhere in the pack, and idempotency is described for the API generally rather than for ingestion specifically. missing for 10: documented backdating/late-arriving event support, ingest-specific idempotency (transaction ID dedup) details, independent or hands-on corroboration of throughput.

support.subject: As a developer, I can stream high-volume usage events — API calls, tokens, compute-seconds — into a metering pipeline with idempotent ingestion and backdating support

citations.quote: Send usage events to Metronome through the /ingest endpoint or by connecting Metronome to Segment.
Metronome's infrastructure supports up to 110,000 events per second (6.6 million events per minute) without requiring pre-aggregation or rollups.
Metronome provides built-in idempotency mechanisms so you can safely retry requests without introducing extraneous data.
